source.title: Measuring Safety Alignment Effects in Autonomous Security Agents

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper text, including results and appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Extends evaluation of less-restricted/abliterated models to autonomous, authorized security agents and reports task success, grounding, and refusal-event rates. It does not implement the original activation-direction intervention.
record.gate_note: The study compares stock instruction models with third-party uncensored or abliterated derivatives. It does not extract, add, or ablate a residual-stream direction, and does not test harmful-request compliance in ordinary chat. It reports zero refusal events for both aligned and less-restricted Gemma conditions in the security-agent setting; this is a floor comparison, not evidence that a derivative removed refusals that were present in its aligned counterpart. Success and grounding comparisons are recorded as findings about the broader subject, not as tests of the direction-specific versions. No result cited from another paper is included as a study result.
record.test_reason: The study uses third-party 'uncensored' and 'abliterated' derivatives as comparison probes and reports their security-agent success, grounding and safety-event rates. It never finds, adds or ablates a direction. It never measures refusal of harmful requests, and in Gemma the aligned models already show 0% refusal events, so refusal removal cannot be seen. Refusal rates for the Qwen and Llama abliterated pairs are not reported. How the TrevorJS Gemma derivatives were made is not stated, and the authors call all derivatives not clean causal counterfactuals. So the results do not bear on whether V2 (or V1) holds.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. Visible refusal does not explain outcomes; the Gemma gains are a broad grounding/capability gap that also appears on coding controls; Qwen does not reproduce the gain; abliterated Llama fails the tool protocol. Derivatives are empirical probes, not causal counterfactuals.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares third-party uncensored or abliterated derivatives with stock instruction models in a multi-turn agent harness. It does not reproduce the original difference-in-means direction discovery or activation projection/addition method.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by model family and derivative provenance; security-agent performance is also sensitive to controller mode and prompt condition. In the 31B strict-versus-repair subset, aligned conditions remain at 0/50 successes, while the uncensored derivative changes from 5/50 under strict to 10/50 under repair. Gemma 31B authorization variants remain at 0/50 successes.

fits_no_version.finding: Less-restricted derivatives change agent success and grounding in a family-dependent way. Gemma derivatives gain (14.0% vs 0.7%; 10.7% vs 0.0%), and similar gains appear on non-security controls. The Qwen abliterated model is slightly lower (2.0% vs 5.3%, p=0.18). The Llama abliterated model collapses (0.0% vs 3.3%; grounding 0.21 vs 2.80; 124/150 vs 35/150 tool failures).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Released abliterated/uncensored derivatives can differ from their parents in general agentic capability, sometimes severely degrading tool-protocol following (Llama 3.1 8B). Abliteration is therefore not reliably capability-neutral in agent settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Unsafe-action rates for less-restricted runs: Gemma 26B 5.3% (aligned 0.0%), Llama 3.3%, Gemma 31B and Qwen 0.0%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Less-restricted derivatives show heterogeneous sandbox-violation rates in authorized security-agent tasks.

record.problems: The paper explicitly cautions that derivative models are not clean causal counterfactuals and may differ through editing, quantization, templates, or provenance. The security suite has 30 tasks and success is near zero for several conditions; grounding is substring-based rather than semantic. Hard-validation reviewer subtype agreement is noisy (κ = 0.35). The reported refusal comparison for Gemma has a zero-rate aligned baseline, limiting inference about refusal removal.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-version result rows were omitted. The paper's strict-versus-repair controller outcomes, prompt-variant success outcomes, task-class breakdowns, and reviewer-audit agreement are not direct measures of the listed direction/refusal versions; key sensitivity findings are summarized in method_sensitivity and problems.

untested.parts: Whether released abliterated or uncensored weights remove refusal on harmful requests. No harmful-request refusal benchmark is run, Gemma refusal is at floor, and Qwen/Llama refusal rates are unreported.
No direction extraction, ablation or addition. Capability is compared only for third-party derivatives of unverified provenance.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T3/'tests' classification and V2 limits_scope label are not justified. Zero refusal on both sides is a floor, not evidence that refusal removal fails or holds. The study cites Arditi et al. only as background for why derivatives exist. The Llama capability collapse may interest V1's 'other abilities kept' clause, but the derivative's construction is not verified, so it is recorded under fits_no_version.

versions.untested_parts: No difference-in-means direction is found, added, or ablated; no causal test of refusal or preservation of general capability using that intervention.

The study compares released uncensored/abliterated derivatives in authorized security-agent tasks, but does not report a direct weight-edit intervention or a harmful-request refusal benchmark. Gemma refusal-event rates are zero in both aligned and less-restricted conditions, so the comparison has a floor effect.
The exploratory jailbreak-style prompt is not shown to suppress the refusal direction; no training against ablation is tested.
No test of affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts.
No separation or measurement of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.
No cross-language or base-to-instruct transfer test of the direction.
No controlled comparison of refusal-training method or timing.

reader_labels.reason: Refusal-event rates are 0.0% for aligned and less-restricted conditions, so these results show no observable refusal removal in this setting and the aligned baseline is already at zero (R1–R6).
